description: In Genesis 47:28 it is stated that Jacob lived for 147 years, of which 17 were spent in Egypt. Jacob's 147 years mark the end of the patriarchal era and the transition to Israel's sojourn in Egypt, a central event in Jewish salvation history. The number carries deep symbolic resonance linked to perfection and divine order, as it is closely connected to the number 7, which in biblical tradition represents wholeness and completion.

versions.meaning: The number 147 is known as the number of years the patriarch Jacob (Israel) lived according to Genesis 47:28.
versions.description: In Genesis 47:28 it is stated that Jacob lived for 147 years, of which 17 were spent in Egypt. The number can be seen as a composition of 7 × 21 (7 × 3 × 7), which reinforces the symbolic meaning of the number 7, representing perfection and wholeness in biblical tradition. Jacob's 147 years mark the end of the patriarchal era and the transition to Israel's sojourn in Egypt, a central event in Jewish salvation history.

footnotes.text: 147 can be decomposed as 7 × 21, that is, 7 × 3 × 7. This structure reinforces the symbolic meaning of the number 7 (perfection) and 3 (divine wholeness), giving Jacob's lifespan a mathematical-symbolic dimension.

Rabbinic tradition (Rashi on Gen 47:28) notes that Jacob spent 17 years in Egypt – the same number of years Joseph spent with his father in Canaan before being sold by his brothers. This symmetry is seen as an expression of divine justice and restoration.
